question: For the previously frozen four-member binary-reward local clipped-GRPO update, how do uniformly sampled one-, two-, and three-label subset estimators compare with full-group audit under matched clean-label cost, and when does the degree-three structure make partial audits biased or variance-inefficient?
prior_work_disclosure: This is a follow-up to the committed order-three Walsh characterization and uses its fixed estimator. The estimator construction is a direct inverse-inclusion application; no algorithmic novelty is asserted.
scope: Exact finite CPU enumeration using only the Python standard library. No model, optimizer, stochastic Monte Carlo, GPU, paid API, or external compute.

estimand.action_space: All 16 vectors under independent Bernoulli(1/4) actions; actions are fully observed.
estimand.reward_space: Y in {0,1}^4 with any declared conditional law given the complete action vector.
estimand.update: G(a,y)=sum_i A_i(y)*(a_i-1/4); A is population-standardized binary group reward, zero for a constant-reward group, as frozen in grpo_audit_order_characterization_v1.
estimand.policy_target: E_A[E[G(A,Y)|A]] under the frozen Bernoulli(1/4) action distribution.

partial_estimators.basis: chi_T(y)=(-1)^(sum_{i in T} y_i), alpha_T(a)=2^-4 sum_y G(a,y) chi_T(y).
partial_estimators.sampling: For each m in {1,2,3}, choose one of the C(4,m) size-m coordinate subsets S uniformly, independently of unobserved clean labels conditional on the observed action.
partial_estimators.estimator: For audit size m, Ghat_m(a,y_S)=sum_{T subseteq S, |T|<=m} alpha_T(a)*chi_T(y)/pi_(m,|T|). For m<3 this is the inverse-inclusion estimator of the degree-m Walsh projection and may be biased for G; for m=3 it is exactly unbiased; m=4 equals G.
partial_estimators.coefficients_disclosure: All estimators use exact coefficients of the fixed mathematical target G, not learned from audited observations. This isolates the information and audit-cost question; it is an oracle-coefficient analysis, not an end-to-end deployable audit procedure.

exact_claims_to_check: For every one of 16 actions, 16 reward vectors, and 4 possible audited triples, the average of Ghat_3 over triples equals G(a,y) exactly.
For arbitrary conditional reward laws, E[Ghat_3|A=a]=E[G|A=a]; this follows from the exhaustive pointwise identity.
For m=1 and m=2, the subset average equals the corresponding degree-m Walsh projection, while m=4 reproduces G exactly.
For each m in {1,2,3,4}, exactly enumerate bias, variance, and mean-squared error under each frozen law; report cost-adjusted MSE m*MSE_m/(4*MSE_4), with zero-baseline cases marked undefined.
For m=3, verify Var(Ghat_3)=Var(G)+E[Var(Ghat_3|A,Y)] for every frozen law; m=1,2 estimates may be biased and are evaluated using MSE, not variance alone.

Two-label observations cannot universally identify the target: re-evaluate the previously frozen P_plus/P_minus order-three parity witness and calculate the exact minimax absolute-bias lower bound for any estimator sharing its observation law.

frozen_conditional_reward_law_grid.independent_bernoulli: For q in {1/5, 1/2, 4/5}, every action stratum uses independent Bernoulli(q) labels.
frozen_conditional_reward_law_grid.common_mode: For q in {1/5, 1/2, 4/5}, Y is all-zero with probability 1-q and all-one with probability q, for every action stratum.
frozen_conditional_reward_law_grid.third_order_parity: For every action a in {0,1}^4, every three-coordinate subset T, epsilon in {1/4,1/2,1}, and sign s in {-1,+1}, the target stratum uses P_s(y|a)=2^-4*(1+s*epsilon*chi_T(y)); every other action stratum is uniform over {0,1}^4. This yields 384 exact cases.

primary_metric: For each law and audit size m, report exact per-group bias and variance. At the frozen 12-label finite budget, use n_m=12/m independent groups and compute exact sample-mean MSE_m=Var(Ghat_m)/n_m+Bias(Ghat_m)^2; compare with full-audit MSE_4=Var(G)/3. Report their ratio. If full-audit MSE is zero, mark ratio undefined. For unbiased m=3, also report the asymptotic variance-per-label-call ratio 3*Var(Ghat_3)/(4*Var(G)). This is a matched clean-label-call comparison, not wall-clock cost.
computation_cost: Alongside label calls, report the exact per-group number of sampled subset choices C(4,m) and Walsh terms evaluated 2^m. These are algorithmic operation counts for the specified estimator, not measured end-to-end latency.

finite_budget_direction_check.budget: Exactly 12 clean-label calls per replicate; m=1,2,3,4 therefore use 12,6,4,3 independent groups respectively.
finite_budget_direction_check.sampling: For each law, arm, and seed, use Python random.Random(seed + 1000003*arm_index + 17*sign_index) to draw independent groups from the frozen action/reward distribution and uniform audit subsets. Report per-seed and pooled wrong-direction-or-zero counts; zero estimates count as direction errors. Report Wilson 95% intervals pooled over the declared repetitions.
finite_budget_direction_check.metric_limit: This is a finite synthetic scalar-gradient direction diagnostic, not a model update or capability measure.

interpretation_rule: Describe a cost-adjusted MSE improvement only for named frozen law cases with R_m<1. Summaries across this constructed finite grid are descriptive; do not generalize to real verifiers, arbitrary workloads, or learned policies. m=1,2 are lower-order projection baselines and can be biased; m=3 is unbiased but can remain inefficient due to audit randomization variance.
claim_limits: No model capability or optimizer outcome is measured.
The target update and action distribution are one previously selected synthetic finite construction; exact target coefficients are supplied to all estimators as an oracle.
The law grid is designed for structural coverage, not as a representative verifier-error distribution.
This does not establish a general adaptive audit algorithm or novelty over related noisy-verifier and audit-allocation literature.
